answer.rationale: Write-path p99 hit 5x starting ~30 minutes after a release, which is the strongest available causal clue; memory_b1 is the closest prior of undoing a bad build without dropping customer writes, so that is the single archive record to confirm before committing. Peak settlement load (memory_b3) is a real alternative explanation, so capacity remains plausible and the release link is not proven. Circuit breaking is rejected because failing fast would sacrifice writes, contrary to the objective. Failover and read-replica routing are weaker fits for a post-release, write-heavy symptom. Downstream settlement value is at risk during this window, so uncertainty is retained pending the b1 source check.
